subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The program counter (PC) holds:
options: The address of the next instruction to be fetched
The result of the last calculation
The instruction currently being decoded
The data most recently read from memory
questions.explain: The program counter stores the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched in the cycle.

questions.q: A variable declared inside a subroutine that is only accessible within that subroutine has which scope?
options: Global scope
Static scope
Local scope
Public scope
questions.explain: A local variable exists only within the subroutine in which it is declared and cannot be accessed outside it.

questions.q: When an interrupt with higher priority occurs, the processor typically:
options: Saves the current state, services the interrupt, then restores the state
Deletes the current program from memory
Ignores it until the current program finishes
Resets the program counter to zero permanently
questions.explain: The CPU saves its current state (registers/PC) onto the stack, runs the ISR, then restores the state to resume.

questions.q: A compiler offers which advantage over an interpreter for distributing finished software?
options: Errors are always reported one at a time during execution
The source code must be shipped with the program
It executes more slowly than interpreted code
It produces machine code that runs without the source or translator present
questions.explain: A compiler produces standalone executable machine code, so the source and translator need not be distributed.

questions.q: GPUs are particularly well suited to which type of task?
options: Tasks requiring very large individual registers and no parallelism
Sequential tasks with many branches
Single-threaded operating system scheduling
Highly parallel tasks performing the same operation on large data sets (e.g. graphics, ML)
questions.explain: GPUs contain many simple cores ideal for data-parallel work like rendering and matrix operations.

questions.q: Selection in programming is implemented by which type of construct?
options: A FOR loop
An IF / CASE statement
An array declaration
A subroutine call
questions.explain: Selection chooses between paths of execution using conditional constructs such as IF or CASE.

questions.q: Excessive swapping of pages between RAM and disk, degrading performance, is known as:
options: Thrashing
Pipelining
Caching
Interleaving
questions.explain: Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions.

questions.q: How does an interpreter differ from a compiler?
options: An interpreter produces a standalone executable file
A compiler executes code without translating it
An interpreter only works on assembly language
An interpreter translates and executes the source line by line at run time
questions.explain: An interpreter translates and executes source code line by line, producing no separate object file.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the stored-program concept?
options: Instructions are stored in memory and can be treated as data, fetched and executed sequentially
Programs can only run from ROM
Programs are hard-wired into the CPU permanently
Each program needs a separate physical processor
questions.explain: The stored-program concept holds that instructions are stored in memory alongside data and executed in sequence.

questions.q: Which statement about passing a parameter by value is correct?
options: Only arrays may be passed this way
The subroutine can permanently alter the caller's original variable
The variable's address is shared with the subroutine
A copy of the data is made, so changes inside the subroutine do not affect the original
questions.explain: By value passes a copy, so modifications within the subroutine leave the caller's original variable unchanged.

questions.q: The 'reduce' (fold) higher-order function is used to:
options: Remove duplicate elements
Return a new list of the same length
Combine the elements of a list into a single accumulated value
Reverse the order of a list
questions.explain: reduce repeatedly applies a combining function to accumulate the list's elements into one result value.

questions.q: Paging divides memory into:
options: Sectors defined by the hard disk geometry
Fixed-size blocks (pages/frames)
Variable-sized logical segments matching program structure
Single contiguous regions per process
questions.explain: Paging splits memory into fixed-size pages (and frames), which need not be contiguous in physical memory.

questions.q: A key characteristic of RISC processors is that they:
options: Use a large, complex set of variable-length instructions
Use a reduced, simple set of instructions that typically execute in one cycle
Have no general-purpose registers
Cannot be pipelined
questions.explain: RISC uses a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions designed to execute quickly, easing pipelining.

questions.q: Compared with iteration, recursion typically uses more of which resource because of the call stack?
options: Network sockets
Cache lines only
Disk bandwidth
Memory
questions.explain: Each recursive call adds a stack frame, so deep recursion consumes more memory than an equivalent loop.

questions.q: Which is a core responsibility of an operating system's memory management?
options: Rendering 3D graphics
Setting the CPU clock frequency
Encrypting all network traffic
Allocating memory to processes and tracking which areas are in use
questions.explain: Memory management allocates and frees memory for processes and keeps track of usage to prevent conflicts.

questions.q: An interrupt is best described as:
options: A permanent halt of the processor
An instruction that doubles clock speed
A type of secondary storage
A signal to the processor indicating an event needs immediate attention
questions.explain: An interrupt is a signal causing the CPU to suspend its current task and service the requesting event.

questions.q: Compared with RISC, CISC architectures tend to:
options: Have fewer addressing modes and simpler instructions
Lack a control unit
Use complex, multi-cycle instructions and require less compiler effort
Always run faster on every workload
questions.explain: CISC provides complex instructions (often multi-cycle), shifting work from the compiler into hardware.

questions.q: Exception handling using a try/catch (try/except) structure is primarily used to:
options: Detect and respond to runtime errors without crashing the program
Define a new class
Speed up loop execution
Declare global constants
questions.explain: Try/catch blocks let a program catch runtime errors and handle them gracefully instead of terminating abnormally.

questions.q: Which of these is a defining feature of pure functional programming?
options: Immutability and functions treated as first-class objects
Sequential modification of state through loops
Heavy use of global mutable variables
Functions with side effects on shared state
questions.explain: Functional programming emphasises immutable data and first-class functions that can be passed and returned like any value.

questions.q: What is meant by describing functions as 'first-class objects' in a language?
options: They must always return an integer
They can only be called from the main program
They execute faster than other code
They can be assigned to variables, passed as arguments and returned from other functions
questions.explain: First-class functions can be stored, passed as parameters, and returned just like any other value.

questions.q: In functional programming, 'immutability' means that:
options: Once created, data values cannot be changed
Programs run without recursion
Functions cannot be passed as arguments
Variables can be freely reassigned
questions.explain: Immutability means data cannot be altered after creation; transformations produce new values instead.

questions.q: In functional programming, the higher-order function 'map' does what?
options: Applies a given function to every element of a list, returning a new list
Sorts a list into ascending order
Reduces a list to a single accumulated value
Selects only elements that satisfy a predicate
questions.explain: map applies a function to each element of a list and returns a new list of the transformed results.

questions.q: Alpha testing differs from beta testing in that alpha testing is:
options: Done automatically by the compiler
Only concerned with performance benchmarking
Carried out in-house by the development team or testers before release to users
Performed by a wide public audience after release
questions.explain: Alpha testing is conducted internally before release, whereas beta testing is done by selected external users.

questions.q: Which paradigm expresses logic as facts and rules, with the system inferring answers to queries (e.g. Prolog)?
options: Imperative
Object-oriented
Declarative/logic programming
Procedural
questions.explain: Logic (declarative) programming states facts and rules and lets an inference engine derive results from queries.

questions.q: Black-box testing is best described as testing that:
options: Is performed only by end users after release
Checks every internal branch and loop of the code
Measures the speed of the program
Tests functionality against the specification without knowledge of the internal code
questions.explain: Black-box testing validates inputs and expected outputs against the spec, treating the implementation as opaque.

questions.q: In a multicore processor, true parallel execution requires that:
options: Only one core is active at a time
The workload can be divided into tasks that run simultaneously on different cores
All cores share a single register only
The clock speed is reduced for each core
questions.explain: Multiple cores give true parallelism only when tasks can be split to run at the same time on separate cores.

questions.q: Which higher-order function returns only the elements of a list that satisfy a given predicate?
options: compose
map
filter
reduce/fold
questions.explain: filter tests each element against a predicate and keeps only those for which it returns true.

questions.q: A record (struct) data type is best described as:
options: A self-referencing subroutine
A collection of elements of the same type accessed by index
A first-in first-out structure
A collection of related fields that may be of different data types
questions.explain: A record groups together several named fields that can hold different data types.

questions.q: A subclass acquiring the attributes and methods of a superclass is an example of which OOP concept?
options: Polymorphism
Abstraction
Inheritance
Encapsulation
questions.explain: Inheritance lets a subclass derive and reuse the attributes and methods defined in its superclass.

questions.q: In object-oriented programming, what does encapsulation primarily achieve?
options: Bundling data and the methods that act on it, hiding internal state behind an interface
Allowing a subclass to acquire attributes and methods of a superclass
Creating multiple instances from one class definition
Allowing one method name to behave differently for different object types
questions.explain: Encapsulation binds attributes and methods together within a class and restricts direct external access to the internal data.
